_comment: NV-119 (2026-09-03, Claude B). Infinitive-form Garo verb used specifically in the modal-'can' construction ('SUBJ [OBJ] VERB-na man·a'). Deliberately a SEPARATE table from purpose_map.json (used for 'want to VERB'/'went to VERB'): the two constructions do not always share a form for the same verb ('work' is 'kam ka·na' here vs purpose_map.json's 'dakna' for the purpose-clause construction; 'go' is 're·angna' here vs purpose_map.json's 're·ang·na', a minor orthographic difference not worth risking by sharing the table). Source: docs/THANGSENG_NATIVE_VALIDATION.md lines ~5943-5945 and ~5757 (native-cited): 'Anga cha·na ama/man·a.' (I can eat), 'Anga re·angna ama/man·a.' (I can go), 'Anga kam ka·na ama/man·a.' (I can work), 'Anga Garo aganna man·a.' (I can speak Garo). Primary variant 'man·a' (not 'ama') per docs/PICKPRIMARY_VERIFIED_TIES.md's existing tie-break for these exact 3 sentences. 'speak' is the ONLY entry with native evidence for an object appearing in this construction (bare, no -ko marker) — do not assume other verbs take an object the same way without their own evidence; see tryModalCanConstruction's own transitive flag. List is intentionally narrow — add only on confirmed evidence, not by inference from this list's existing entries or from purpose_map.json.
